title: Dental checkup and cleaning
what: A dentist checks your teeth and gums, and a hygienist removes tartar and plaque. This is done with special tools and a gentle powder.
why: Usually every 6 to 12 months, for prevention. Also for bleeding gums, bad breath, and before treatment or braces.
tell_doctor: Heart disease, artificial heart valves, or a pacemaker
Allergies to medicines or numbing shots
If your teeth are sensitive to cold

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can eat as usual. Brush your teeth before your visit.

prepare.title: Sensitivity
prepare.text: If your teeth are sensitive, say so ahead of time. They can numb them or use a gentler setting.

bring: Dental x-rays, if you have them
A list of the medicines you take
steps: The dentist checks your teeth and gums and takes an x-ray if needed
An ultrasonic tool removes the tartar
A spray of water and powder removes plaque and stains
Your teeth are polished with paste
Sometimes a protective fluoride coating is put on
The dentist explains how to care for your teeth at home
feel: Your gums may bleed a little. This is normal if they are inflamed
If it feels unpleasant or hurts, raise your hand and they will pause
after: Usually for 1 to 2 hours, do not eat or drink things that stain: coffee, tea, wine
For a few days, your teeth may be sensitive to cold
Gums usually stop bleeding in 1 to 2 weeks

faq.a: No. The tools remove tartar and plaque, not enamel. Sensitivity after cleaning usually passes in a few days.

faq.q: How often do I need a professional cleaning?
faq.a: Usually every 6 months. With braces, gum disease, or a lot of tartar, your dentist may advise more often.
